To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the network effects of hypertext systems are a function of the control assumptions of the system.
the network effects of hypertext systems can be positive, negative, or neutral, depending on the control choices that are made in the design of a system.
The control choices made by a hypertext system affect its incentive structures, and thus affect the amount of content and users in the system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and implementation of a hypertext-based, open, collaborative environment.
the development of a hypertext model that is based on the idea that a document consists of a network of nodes that are linked together.
the development of an open hypermedia system for the World-Wide Web, which is based on the Open Hypermedia System Architecture (OHSA).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
hypertext systems are a very important part of the future of computing and the future of the Internet.
the network effects of the Web are not as strong as those of other media, such as television, and are much weaker than those of the telephone.
the Web is a hypertext system that exhibits network effects and that the network effects of the Web have been a significant factor in its success.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the control assumptions of the Web are the most conducive to network effects, while the control assumptions of monolithic hypertexts are the least conducive to network effects.
the network effect of the Web has been so powerful that it is now the only hypertext system that matters.
the Web has a much more complex incentive structure, but that the Web is also much more open than monolithic hypertext and open hypermedia systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Web is not a good example of a networked hypertext system, but rather an example of an open hypermedia system.
the network effects in hypertex systems can be harnessed to create incentives for content creation, and that these incentives can be tuned by the choice of underlying control assumptions.
control choices can have a profound effect on the network effects of a hypertext-based system, and thus its success.
